answer: Escalating per-identity rent. Identity n pays a recurring fee f(n)=b(1+αn^β), due every epoch; unpaid identities lose task-submission and payout rights. Fees settle in quartz, so each extra identity’s rent is a real recurring charge. The public ledger records every payment under an ivory seal. An attacker registering k identities pays Σf(n), which rises superlinearly, and high n leaves no cheap haven.
